findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body: After callers invoke the returned cleanup function, the handler remains registered and continues receiving messages. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles therefore retain handlers, cause duplicate processing, and increase memory and per-message work. The removed `socket.off("message", handler)` call previously provided the cleanup contract.

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the cleanup callback
findings.body:
For any socket receiving a `"message"` after the returned cleanup is called, the supposedly detached handler still executes. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles also accumulate handlers, causing duplicate processing and listener leaks.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the returned cleanup function
findings.body:
For any socket emitting `"message"` after the returned disposer is called, the handler remains registered and is invoked after teardown. Repeated attach/dispose cycles also accumulate duplicate listeners, breaking the existing cleanup contract and causing leaks or duplicate processing.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
On a long-lived or reused socket, calling the returned disposer no longer revokes the handler. Any subsequent peer-controlled `message` still reaches a stale handler, potentially crossing session, tenant, or authorization boundaries and acting on captured privileged state after teardown.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
When callers invoke the returned cleanup while the socket remains alive, the `"message"` listener stays registered and retains its handler. Repeated attach/cleanup cycles accumulate listeners, causing unbounded memory growth, duplicate message processing, and increasing per-message work.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
